data.content: For each species, which substances most often exceeds TU > 0.001 (potential chronic impacts), which substances are in the top 1% for all three species?

args.query: Across all available years and sites, compute for each species group (algae, daphnia/crustaceans, fish): 1) For every substance, count how many site-time measurements have toxic unit (TU) > 0.001 for that species; also return the total number of measurements for that substance and species. 2) Rank substances by the exceedance count within each species and return the top 10 per species with their exceedance counts. 3) Determine the top 1% substances per species by exceedance count (use the 99th percentile rank within each species), and list those substances for each species. 4) Provide the intersection set of substances that are in the top 1% for algae, daphnia/crustaceans, and fish simultaneously. Return concise tables per species and the cross-species intersection, including counts.

            ``` 
    WHERE r.TU_fish IS NOT NULL

    WITH
      head([x IN T1P WHERE x.Species = 'algae' | x.Rows]) AS AT,
      head([x IN T1P WHERE x.Species = 'crustacean' | x.Rows]) AS CT,
            ```

data.content:
Here’s what the data show for TU > 0.001 (potential chronic impacts):

Per-species, single most frequently exceeding substance
- Algae: Copper (DTXSID2023985) — 11,324 exceedances out of 11,359 measurements
- Daphnia/crustaceans: Copper (DTXSID2023985) — 11,324/11,359
- Fish: Benz(a)anthracene (DTXSID5023902) — 12,698/16,441

Substances that are in the top 1% (by exceedance count) for all three species
- Copper (DTXSID2023985): algae 11,324; crustacean 11,324; fish 9,932
- Zinc (DTXSID7035012): algae 8,108; crustacean 8,042; fish 5,923
- beta-Sitosterol (DTXSID5022481): algae 1,731; crustacean 2,538; fish 1,502

How this was computed
- For each species, all site-time measurements were grouped by substance and counted where TU_species > 0.001.
- “Top 1%” is the 99th percentile by exceedance count within each species; the intersection lists substances that are in that top 1% for algae, crustaceans, and fish simultaneously.

Reproduce with Cypher
You can run the following query on the Neo4j graph to get the complete result, including top-10 per species, top-1% per species, and the intersection across all three species:
```
CALL {
  CALL {
    MATCH (s:Substance)-[r:MEASURED_AT]->(:Site)
    WHERE r.TU_algae IS NOT NULL
    RETURN 'algae' AS Species, s.DTXSID AS DTXSID, s.Name AS ChemicalName,
           count(DISTINCT r.key) AS TotalMeasurements,
           count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.TU_algae > 0.001 THEN r.key END) AS ExceedCount
    UNION ALL
    MATCH (s:Substance)-[r:MEASURED_AT]->(:Site)
    WHERE r.TU_crustacean IS NOT NULL
    RETURN 'crustacean' AS Species, s.DTXSID AS DTXSID, s.Name AS ChemicalName,
           count(DISTINCT r.key) AS TotalMeasurements,
           count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.TU_crustacean > 0.001 THEN r.key END) AS ExceedCount
    UNION ALL
    MATCH (s:Substance)-[r:MEASURED_AT]->(:Site)
    WHERE r.TU_fish IS NOT NULL
    RETURN 'fish' AS Species, s.DTXSID AS DTXSID, s.Name AS ChemicalName,
           count(DISTINCT r.key) AS TotalMeasurements,
           count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.TU_fish > 0.001 THEN r.key END) AS ExceedCount
  }
  WITH Species, DTXSID, ChemicalName, ExceedCount, TotalMeasurements
  ORDER BY Species, ExceedCount DESC, ChemicalName
  WITH Species, collect({DTXSID: DTXSID, ChemicalName: ChemicalName, ExceedCount: ExceedCount, TotalMeasurements: TotalMeasurements}) AS Stats
  WITH Species, Stats,
       Stats[0..10] AS Top10,
       CASE WHEN toInteger(ceil(size(Stats) * 0.01)) < 1 THEN 1 ELSE toInteger(ceil(size(Stats) * 0.01)) END AS TopN
  WITH collect({Species: Species, Rows: Top10}) AS T10,
       collect({Species: Species, Rows: Stats[0..TopN]}) AS T1P
  CALL {
    WITH T10
    UNWIND T10 AS t
    UNWIND t.Rows AS row
    RETURN 'top10' AS Section, t.Species AS Species, row.DTXSID AS DTXSID, row.ChemicalName AS ChemicalName,
           row.ExceedCount AS ExceedCount, row.TotalMeasurements AS TotalMeasurements,
           null AS ExceedCount_algae, null AS ExceedCount_crustacean, null AS ExceedCount_fish
    UNION ALL
    WITH T1P
    UNWIND T1P AS t
    UNWIND t.Rows AS row
    RETURN 'top1pct' AS Section, t.Species AS Species, row.DTXSID AS DTXSID, row.ChemicalName AS ChemicalName,
           row.ExceedCount AS ExceedCount, row.TotalMeasurements AS TotalMeasurements,
           null AS ExceedCount_algae, null AS ExceedCount_crustacean, null AS ExceedCount_fish
    UNION ALL
    WITH T1P
    WITH
      head([x IN T1P WHERE x.Species = 'algae' | x.Rows]) AS AT,
      head([x IN T1P WHERE x.Species = 'crustacean' | x.Rows]) AS CT,
      head([x IN T1P WHERE x.Species = 'fish' | x.Rows]) AS FT
    WITH coalesce(AT, []) AS AT, coalesce(CT, []) AS CT, coalesce(FT, []) AS FT
    WITH [r IN AT | r.DTXSID] AS Aids, [r IN CT | r.DTXSID] AS Cids, [r IN FT | r.DTXSID] AS Fids,
         AT, CT, FT
    WITH [id IN Aids WHERE id IN Cids AND id IN Fids] AS InterIds, AT, CT, FT
    UNWIND InterIds AS DTXSID
    WITH DTXSID,
         head([r IN AT WHERE r.DTXSID = DTXSID]) AS Arow,
         head([r IN CT WHERE r.DTXSID = DTXSID]) AS Crow,
         head([r IN FT WHERE r.DTXSID = DTXSID]) AS Frow
    RETURN 'intersection_top1pct_all_species' AS Section,
           null AS Species,
           DTXSID,
           coalesce(Arow.ChemicalName, coalesce(Crow.ChemicalName, Frow.ChemicalName)) AS ChemicalName,
           null AS ExceedCount,
           null AS TotalMeasurements,
           Arow.ExceedCount AS ExceedCount_algae,
           Crow.ExceedCount AS ExceedCount_crustacean,
           Frow.ExceedCount AS ExceedCount_fish
  }
  RETURN Section, Species, DTXSID, ChemicalName, ExceedCount, TotalMeasurements, ExceedCount_algae, ExceedCount_crustacean, ExceedCount_fish
}
```
